reason: The examples all mean borne in pairs (inflorescences at a node, spikelets, stipules); FLOPO paired already has 'in pairs' and 'geminate'. The other sense, a leaf of two leaflets, does not occur here.
'Stems pseudobulbous (at base)' says the stem forms a pseudobulb; PO lists pseudobulb as a synonym of corm.

The Raunkiaer life form already exists as the growth-form phenotype class FLOPO:0900024, which is a phenotype class, not a 0991 value class. 'Géofrutex' (a geoxylic subshrub) is a different growth form and should not be mapped here.
Beadlike glomerules, sori and segments = like a string of beads: FLOPO moniliform.
Rhizomes, stems, scapes and roots buried in the ground = below the ground surface. 'Sori buried in tomentum' is a different sense and should not be mapped.

label: acrostichoid
definition: A spatial pattern quality inhering in the sporangia of a fern leaf by virtue of their covering the whole abaxial surface of the fertile lamina instead of being grouped into discrete sori.
reason: A standard pteridological term with no PATO or FLOPO equivalent; it inheres in the sporangia or the soral area.
A compound of two values of moss laminal cells: linear (PATO) and flexuous (= PATO:0001989 sinuous, per the earlier rule).
Inflorescences or flowers opposite to leaves = leaf-opposed. The FLOPO class exists, so the relation pattern is not needed.
Long-lasting flowers, petals and inflorescences = remaining for a long time; PATO has no 'persistent', and non-deciduous does not fit flowers that last.
Tuberlike roots and root thickenings = thickened like a tuber: FLOPO tuberous.

Most statements are about Apiaceae fruits and furrows bearing vittae (oil canals), a FLOPO anatomy class; '3-vittate' is a count of parts. 'Vittate claw' and striped perianth segments mean striped (PATO_0001946 banded) and need their own bearer-restricted rule.
Leaves, stipules, bracts and sepal bases embracing the stem or lip = partially enclosing it: PATO clasping. FLOPO amplexicaul is narrower (stem-clasping leaf bases).
Goniautoicous is the form of autoicy in which the perigonia are bud-like in the axils of the female branches. FLOPO autoicous is its direct parent, and a separate child class is not needed yet.
A compound of two cell shapes (linear and rectangular), not a single quality.
A pseudopanicle is an inflorescence that resembles a panicle without strictly being one, which is exactly FLOPO panicle-like.
A compound of two inflorescence values: corymb-like (PATO_0002455) and cymose.
Stipe is a synonym of stalk (rule C264), so stipeless = stalk absent.
A compound of two margin values: undulate (PATO_0000967) and dentate.
A heterocotylous embryo has cotyledons of unequal size: FLOPO unequal on the cotyledons, the same model as unequal sepals.
The keel of lemmas and fruits is a ridge (carinate = keel-shaped, rule C221). PO keel PO_0025327 means the corolla keel of legumes and does not apply here.
Barbellulate means minutely barbellate (pappus bristles with tiny barbs). The existing barbellate class covers it; a separate diminutive class is not needed.
Seeds without an aril.

Pea-like flowers or corollas are papilionaceous; PO defines keel as part of the papilionaceous corolla, so its presence captures the type. 'Fruit pea-like' means pea-sized (FLOPO:0991041) and needs its own rule.
'Semi-' weakens the value like 'sub-' or '±': approximately prostrate. Decumbent (PATO_0002343) would claim ascending tips, which the source does not state.
Negates the existing FLOPO value gland-dotted.
FLOPO virgate has 'broom-like' as a synonym and covers plants, branches and inflorescences. The corona-appendage use is a minority and should be checked.
Negates the existing FLOPO value crested.
The mirror of the rule for 'veined' (C211, vascular bundle present). Where the source means 'veins not visible', PATO inconspicuous would be the safer reading, so a bearer check is advised.
A cleistocarpous moss capsule has no operculum and does not open along a regular line; it releases its spores only as it decays: an indehiscent capsule.

label: extravaginal
definition: A positional quality inhering in a lateral shoot of a grass or sedge by virtue of its breaking through the base of the subtending leaf sheath, instead of growing up inside it.
reason: A standard grass and sedge character for innovations and tillers with no PATO or FLOPO term. Its opposite, intravaginal, also appears in the candidates.
